name: F.C.S. Schiller
biography: A modern (early twentieth-century) founder of pragmatism who called himself a disciple of Protagoras, drawing on the Theaetetus's suggestion that one opinion can be 'better' than another even if not 'truer.' Named as one of the three protagonists of pragmatism alongside James and Dewey, but noted by Russell to be of lesser importance than the other two.
